Send a notifications/progress every [runs].progress_s (default 30) from the offload relay itself (not only per log line), for any call carrying a progressToken. data.body:
Operator 2026-10-19: review commands exceed the agent<->MCP call timeout (a review is 4-45 min on the LAN hosts) so agents start them as background shell processes and poll output files by hand. Interim, concrete fix that does not wait for the research (RM-long-ops-research, P-remote.runs): ddflow review gets --detach (and the MCP tool a [review].sync_wait_s knob, default well under the client timeout): start the review as a ddflow job (ddflow job run, survives the caller), return {run key, log path, started_at, poll_after_s}, record gate.started, keep the lease renewed (DX-long-op-renew), and record the outcome when it ends. A retry with the same item+head joins the same run (idempotent key). Poll with the existing wait/status surface (bounded long-poll). Regression test: a review that outlasts sync_wait_s returns a handle and a later poll yields the recorded outcome; a second identical call joins, not duplicates. Reuse the job engine and DX-gate-run-detach's runner; do not add a process manager. Order: share the detach runner with DX-gate-run-detach.

REFINED by RM-long-ops-research (docs/ddflow/research/mcp-long-ops.md, 2026-10-19): do not build a review-specific runner; build on RM-runs-core. sync_wait_s default 20 s (below Codex's 60 s tool_timeout_sec default per its docs); the handle is {run,op,item,head,state,started_at,elapsed_s,eta_s,poll_after_s,log,pid,host}; run key = sha256(review|item|head|reviewer set|args)[:16], a second identical call JOINS (alive pid) or returns the recorded result; poll with ddflow_run wait_s<=45 (RM-run-tool-mcp); the worker renews the lease, the caller need not; a dead pid without outcome records the gate unavailable, never passed. Also emit progress while waiting (RM-progress-everywhere). Falsifier result: progress alone fixes only Claude Code's idle timer (probed), not other clients, so the handle stays.

The unit_tests gate runner times out on the full suite (about 7 minutes, longer under load), so agents ran the suite themselves and recorded unit_tests by hand; the ci gate also blocks a shell for 10-20 minutes. Run a gate command as a detached ddflow job (the job engine exists: ddflow job run) with its log path, renew the lease while it runs, record the gate outcome from the exit code when it finishes, and report in status/brief that it is in flight; --wait attaches to it. Regression test: a gate command that sleeps beyond the old timeout is recorded passed when it exits 0, with its log kept.

Filed 2026-10-15 from use (D-file-ddflow-defects). CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-company-workflows): every number a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; defaults overridable per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

FOLDED IN from DX-gate-background-limit (2026-10-16 roadmap review, duplicate of this task): Gate runs over MCP hit a 30 minute background limit regardless of gate timeout_s
Bug Bec9936dc6b second half: unit_tests under load exceeded the 30m background limit. The command/timeout are already configurable ([gate.unit_tests].command/timeout_s); the fixed 30m cap of the background runner is not. Make the cap a config knob or have the gate survive it.

REFINED by RM-long-ops-research (docs/ddflow/research/mcp-long-ops.md): (1) the '30 minute background limit' is very likely Claude Code's 30 min stdio IDLE window (CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT, probed: a silent call aborts), not a ddflow constant (none found in services/gates): ddflow_gate_run/ddflow_ci send no progress at all; RM-progress-everywhere fixes that first. (2) --detach and [gate].sync_wait_s (default 20) sit on RM-runs-core: same run key (gate|item|head|command digest), same handle, same ddflow_run poll; reuse the started-marker and dead_runs. (3) --wait attaches to the run by key. Regression additionally: a second identical gate run on the same head joins the live run.

Gates, reviews, merges, lane starts and exports take minutes. A call returns a run handle (key derived from the request so a retry joins the same run), GET /v1/runs/<key> and events report progress, the MCP tasks extension is used by clients that support it and polling by the rest. Built on ddflow job run (detached, survives the caller) and the log; no new process manager.

REFINED by RM-long-ops-research (docs/ddflow/research/mcp-long-ops.md): RM-runs-core is the local engine and handle schema; this task exposes it: GET /v1/runs/<key>, events, and the MCP tasks mapping. Handle fields are task-compatible (run=taskId, state working|input_required|completed|failed|cancelled, poll_after_s=pollIntervalMs, ttl_s=ttlMs). Return resultType:'task' ONLY to a client that declared io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in per-request clientCapabilities (2026-07-28 ext; as of the MCP client matrix no probed client does), else the plain handle + ddflow_run. 2025-11-25 core tasks (task param, tasks/result blocking) are experimental and need not be implemented. Keep key idempotency, which MCP tasks lack.

From the roborev speed research (2026-10-02; 126 jobs measured): a roborev job takes a median 299 s and p90 963 s, plus queue wait; an agent running 'roborev review --wait' holds its item's lease and file globs throughout (mcp.py was held 40-65 min per task). Design: 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async' enqueues the job (roborev review <sha> without --wait), records the gate PENDING with the roborev job id, and returns at once; 'ddflow gate collect <id> standards' reads the job's STATUS (never the exit code: 'roborev review --wait -q' exits 1 for findings OR any failure) and records passed / failed(with findings) / unavailable (errored, canceled, timed out, no review stored). Merge and complete refuse while the gate is pending ('pending is not passed'). Leases renew while the item has pending jobs. Acceptance: pending is recorded with the job id and returns in < 5 s; a canceled, errored, timed-out or no-review job collects as unavailable, never passed; merge and complete refuse while pending; a regression test fails against the synchronous gate; CLI and MCP parity test. Reference: roborev wait --job N, roborev show --job N (a review stored after a wrapper timeout is still retrievable).

Absorbed 2026-10-10 from B-roborev-wait-by-job (same design, the driver-text half): the implement driver and every per-agent delta say: run 'roborev review <sha>' WITHOUT --wait (or 'ddflow gate run <id> standards --async'), then wait by job id ('roborev wait --job N') with ddflow heartbeats at least every 10 min; read the result with 'roborev show --job N' even after a timeout (job 943 ran 27 min and its review was still retrievable); never trust the exit code of 'roborev review --wait -q' (1 = findings OR any failure), read the job status; review only the new tip (range jobs run 2.7x longer than single commits) unless a merge interaction is the point; do not hold file globs longer than the code edit needs. Acceptance: driver and every per-agent delta say so; the help-consistency test passes and every command named exists. B-res-inflight-gates (P-resume) tracks roborev async jobs by job id on restart; this task ships the gate verbs and the driver text.

REFINED by RM-long-ops-research: implement the async standards gate as a run of op 'standards' on RM-runs-core (worker = roborev wait --job N, key = standards|item|sha); gate collect = ddflow_run wait; do not build a separate pending mechanism. Acceptance unchanged.
